gates.name: Pester (Windows)
gates.stops: A failing assertion in any of the 11 Pester suites named in the job's $files list (installer helpers, redaction, supply-chain pinning, SHA gate), run under pwsh on windows-latest.
would_not_stop: A Pester suite that exists but is not in the hard-coded $files list: a new scripts/pester.*.tests.ps1 is silently never run.
Behaviour that differs under Windows PowerShell 5.1, which many students run: the job uses pwsh 7.
Real installs over the network: the suites test wrapper logic, not that Sentinel / Overmind / the extractor actually install.
Any behaviour no suite asserts.
gates.source: .github/workflows/test.yml header comment and the job's $files list.

gates.name: Bash tests (Ubuntu)
gates.stops: A failing case in tests/test-install-sh.bash or tests/test-handoff-locale.bash (install.sh helpers, redaction, pinning, dot-source hygiene).
would_not_stop: tests/test-new-layers.bash: it is in tests/ but no CI step runs it.
macOS bash 3.2 incompatibilities: the job runs Ubuntu's bash only.
A broken real install of Sentinel or Overmind: per the workflow header, they are deliberately not pip-installed in CI; only wrapper logic is tested.
gates.source: .github/workflows/test.yml header comment; tests/ listing.

gates.name: Python tests (Ubuntu)
gates.stops: A failing pytest test anywhere under tests/, on Python 3.11 on Ubuntu -- including tests/test_gate_gaps.py, which is what enforces this registry. Since port S-D: an install of pytest or any dependency that is not hash-pinned in requirements-ci.lock (pip --require-hashes refuses a missing or mismatched hash); tests/test_ci_lock.py refuses any unpinned `pip install` added to the workflow.
would_not_stop: scripts/test_recall.py and scripts/test_refresh_pins.py: they live outside tests/ and `pytest tests/` does not collect them.
Windows-only path or encoding behaviour, and any other Python version.
A test that is skipped or xfailed: pytest reports those without failing the job.
A weak test that passes whatever the code does (that is scripts/blank-and-rerun.py's question).
A malicious or broken package version that a PR deliberately pins with its real hash: the lock proves integrity of the bytes, not their trustworthiness -- lock bumps need review.
pip itself, which comes from the runner's setup-python image and is not pinned by the lock.
gates.source: .github/workflows/test.yml python-tests job; scripts/ listing. Port S-D report (requirements-ci.lock, tests/test_ci_lock.py).

gates.name: HASH files in sync with install scripts
gates.stops: A PR where install/install.ps1 or install/install.sh no longer matches the SHA-256 recorded in docs/HASH.txt / docs/HASH-linux.txt (a stale hash breaks every fresh install's self-check).
would_not_stop: A malicious or broken installer committed together with its regenerated hash: the check proves the two files agree, not that the installer is safe.
Drift in any other downloadable file (bootstrap/e156-setup.*, docs/e156-setup.*, docs/bootstrap.ps1): only the two install scripts are hashed.
The copy actually served from GitHub Pages differing from the repo copy.
gates.source: scripts/regen-hashes.sh header; .github/workflows/test.yml hash-check job.

gates.name: i18n landing pages match English structure
gates.stops: An English docs/index.html whose count of <details> blocks differs from docs/fr, pt, ar or ur index.html (the 2026-04-27 regression where non-English students lost four sections).
would_not_stop: docs/sw/index.html: Swahili is not in the checked language list (it has 0 <details> blocks against English's 5 at the time of sealing, and passes).
Translation quality or content: equal counts of different or untranslated sections pass.
Any i18n page other than index.html.
gates.source: scripts/check-i18n-parity.sh header ('We don't validate translation quality') and its langs=(fr pt ar ur) list.

gates.name: Pages link-check (lychee)
gates.stops: A dead link or broken #fragment anchor in docs/**/*.html before it reaches the Pages surface.
would_not_stop: Broken links in README.md or any other Markdown: the scope is docs/**/*.html only, by design.
A dead site answering 403 or 429: both are in the --accept list and count as alive.
A link that resolves to the wrong or changed content.
gates.source: .github/workflows/test.yml link-check job comments and args.

gates.name: Static analysis (ShellCheck + PSScriptAnalyzer)
gates.stops: An error-severity ShellCheck finding in the 9 listed .sh files, or an Error-severity PSScriptAnalyzer finding in install/, scripts/, bootstrap/, docs/.
would_not_stop: Warning- or style-level findings (e.g. SC2034, SC2155): --severity=error by design.
.sh files not in the explicit list, e.g. scripts/install-aact*.sh, install-pairwise70.sh, install-rapidmeta.sh, install-e156-capsules.sh, regen-hashes.sh, check-i18n-parity.sh, and all tests/*.bash.
PSAvoidUsingWriteHost and PSUseShouldProcessForStateChangingFunctions: excluded.
Logic bugs a linter cannot see.
gates.source: .github/workflows/test.yml lint job comments and file list.

gates.name: Teaching 1-pager Sentinel list matches Sentinel repo (DISABLED: if: false)
gates.stops: Nothing. The job is `if: false`: it never runs, on any push or PR. It exists to make the dependency visible.
would_not_stop: Drift between the auto-generated Sentinel rule list in docs/teaching/intro-1pager.md and the real Sentinel repo -- the exact error (fabricated rule IDs) the generator was written to prevent -- unless a maintainer runs `bash scripts/regen-sentinel-rule-list.sh --check` locally before the PR.
Anything at all: a green CI run says nothing about this check.
gates.source: .github/workflows/test.yml comment above `if: false`; scripts/regen-sentinel-rule-list.sh header.

gates.name: protect-test-config (opt-in PreToolUse hook)
gates.stops: An agent editing test setup/config (conftest.py, pytest.ini, tox.ini, noxfile.py, .coveragerc, jest/vitest/karma/mocha config, phpunit.xml, testthat setup/helper files) through Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit or a write-shaped Bash command -- only where a user has installed the hook.
would_not_stop: Anything, unless the user opted in: nothing in the starter installs it.
A Bash command that builds the file name at runtime (python -c "open(...)"): Bash detection is a heuristic on name + write-shaped operator.
Edits to the TEST FILES themselves (test_*.py); agents legitimately add tests, so review test diffs.
What a human commits; pair it with code review.
pyproject.toml / setup.cfg test settings unless E156_PROTECT_PYPROJECT=1.
Malformed hook input: exit 1 is fail-OPEN by design (Claude Code does not block).
gates.source: scripts/protect-test-config.py docstring 'WHAT IT DOES NOT CHECK', 'OPTIONAL WIDER SCOPE' and 'EXIT CODES'.

gates.name: blank-and-rerun
gates.stops: A claim that the tests cover function X when replacing X's body with `raise NotImplementedError` leaves them green (CLAIM-FAILS, exit 1); a suite that fails before blanking is INCONCLUSIVE (exit 2), never a pass.
would_not_stop: Wrong numbers: TESTS-BITE means the tests notice the function is gone, not that its output is right. Pair with a known-answer test against R.
R functions: Python only; blank R by hand and rerun testthat.
An installed (pip / editable) copy shadowing the blanked one: every function then 'survives' -- errs toward CLAIM-FAILS, never a false pass.
An absolute path in --cmd that points back at the real files.
Anything, unless someone runs it: no CI job or hook calls it.
gates.source: scripts/blank-and-rerun.py docstring 'WHAT IT DOES NOT CHECK'.

gates.name: pass-to-pass
gates.stops: A change after which a pytest test that passed in the BEFORE snapshot now fails, errors, is skipped at run time, or no longer runs (REGRESSED, exit 1); no result file, no tests run, nothing passing before, or a timeout is INCONCLUSIVE (exit 2), never a pass.
would_not_stop: A test edited to assert less: outcomes are compared, not test contents (read test diffs; pair with scripts/blank-and-rerun.py).
A regression in code no test covers.
Non-pytest suites (anything that cannot write JUnit XML through --junitxml).
A regression hidden by running a different --cmd for the BEFORE snapshot: the snapshot is only as wide as the command that made it.
Anything, unless someone runs it: no CI job or hook calls it.
gates.source: scripts/pass-to-pass.py docstring 'WHAT IT DOES NOT CHECK'; docs/AGENT-TEST-INTEGRITY.md section 3.

gates.name: check-i18n-parity
gates.stops: A <details>-count mismatch between docs/index.html and docs/{fr,pt,ar,ur}/index.html (exit 1), or a missing English page (exit 2).
would_not_stop: docs/sw/index.html, which is not in langs=(fr pt ar ur).
Translation quality: structural parity only, stated in its own header.
Equal counts of different sections.
gates.source: scripts/check-i18n-parity.sh header 'What it checks'.

gates.name: gate-can-fail
gates.stops: A file named *_gate.py (or another --suffix) with no reachable non-zero exit -- a 'gate' that can only pass (DEFECTS-FOUND, exit 1).
would_not_stop: A gate whose failing exit is syntactically present but unreachable (`if False: sys.exit(1)`): reachability is judged syntactically.
Whether any real input reaches the failing exit -- that is a known-answer test, a different instrument.
Files outside the naming convention: the default scope is a NAME, and a name-scoped rule retires itself as names drift (230 verdict-returning files, 42 unable to fail, none named *_gate.py).
Anything, unless someone runs it: no CI job or hook calls it.
gates.source: scripts/gate-can-fail.py docstring 'WHAT IT DOES NOT CHECK' and 'THE DEFAULT SCOPE IS A NAME'.

gates.name: pooled-point-achievable
gates.stops: A served pooled point outside the hull of the per-trial effects (no estimator can produce it), or -- when an inverse-variance method is declared via --method -- outside the random-effects tau-path (DEFECTS-FOUND, exit 1).
would_not_stop: A reachable but wrong number: ACHIEVABLE bounds arithmetic, not provenance; it does not mean the point was computed from these trials.
Mantel-Haenszel, Peto or bespoke fixed weightings inside the hull: limb 2 does not exclude them, and without --method it does not set the exit code.
Transcription errors in the per-trial effects you typed in.
Anything, unless someone runs it: no CI job or hook calls it.
gates.source: scripts/pooled-point-achievable.py docstring 'What a CLEAN verdict here does and does not mean'.

gates.name: refresh-ecosystem-pins --check
gates.stops: A 40-hex install-layer pin that lags its source repo's remote HEAD, or a layer whose ls-remote failed (exit 1 in --check).
would_not_stop: Tag-pinned layers: they are skipped. As of 2026-06-08 every layer is tag-pinned, so --check reports all [skip] and passes by construction.
Whether the remote commit it would move to is trustworthy: it moves pins forward, it does not review them.
Anything in CI: it needs the network and no CI job runs it.
gates.source: scripts/refresh-ecosystem-pins.py docstring 'Design guarantees'.

gates.name: regen-hashes --check
gates.stops: docs/HASH.txt or docs/HASH-linux.txt differing from the SHA-256 of install/install.ps1 / install/install.sh (exit 1 in --check).
would_not_stop: A bad installer committed with its regenerated hash (write mode makes the two agree by definition).
Any downloadable file other than the two install scripts.
gates.source: scripts/regen-hashes.sh header.

gates.name: regen-sentinel-rule-list --check
gates.stops: The Sentinel rule list in docs/teaching/intro-1pager.md drifting from a local Sentinel checkout (exit 1 in --check).
would_not_stop: Drift when no Sentinel checkout is found: exit 2, and the only CI job that would run it is `if: false` (see the declared gap above).
A stale local Sentinel checkout: it compares against whatever copy it finds first, not the published repo.
gates.source: scripts/regen-sentinel-rule-list.sh header 'Source of truth' and 'Exit codes'.

gates.name: render-gate-gaps --check (this registry)
gates.stops: A workflow job or check script with no entry here, an orphan entry, a kind contradicting the code (e.g. an `if: false` job registered as a gate), a seal that no longer matches the gate's bytes, or a stale docs/GATE_GAPS.md (exit 1). Enforced in CI by tests/test_gate_gaps.py.
would_not_stop: Untrue or incomplete gap lists: the seal proves someone re-sealed after the last change, not that they re-read anything.
Gates outside its enumeration: PowerShell scripts, install/ and bootstrap/, scripts/ subfolders, and git hooks installed by other tools (Sentinel pre-push).
A checker script with no --check/--selftest mode, no hook payload, and no direct CI invocation.
Whether a gate CAN fail: it runs no gate.
gates.source: scripts/render-gate-gaps.py docstring 'WHAT IT DOES NOT CHECK'.

gates.name: search-record-reconcile
gates.stops: A search record whose identifier list, distinct identifiers, per-page sum and reported total do not all agree -- an unexhausted cursor, a page transcribed short or twice, or a duplicated identifier (exit 1).
would_not_stop: Wrong identifiers or a badly aimed query: it compares a record against itself, so a record whose stated numbers are both untrue passes.
Records that name no identifiers: NOT_ASSESSABLE, counted separately, never a pass -- but never a refusal either.
Low recall: whether the search found the trials that exist is a different measurement (docs/SEARCH-COMPLETENESS.md).
Anything, unless someone runs it: no CI job or hook calls it.
gates.source: scripts/search-record-reconcile.py docstring 'WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH'.

gates.name: trial-identity-screen
gates.stops: An included-studies table where one trial appears more than once, detected from denominators (arm-level and total subset-sums, near-duplicates within a transcription tolerance, the I-squared co-signature) -- DEFECTS-FOUND, exit 1.
would_not_stop: Trials of similar size that collide by coincidence: it is a screen, not a verdict; every hit needs reading.
Denominator inflation, unless you supply --universe: the screen cannot know it.
Tables beyond the subset-sum bounds (40 rows, subsets of 4): those are INCONCLUSIVE, not checked.
A duplicate entered with different denominators (e.g. a later follow-up): names and citation strings are ignored by design.
Anything, unless someone runs it: no CI job or hook calls it.
gates.source: scripts/trial-identity-screen.py docstring and constants MAX_ROWS_FOR_SUBSET_SUM / MAX_SUBSET_SIZE.

gates.name: honest-ratchet (protective state may only get quieter with a named acknowledgement)
gates.stops: A change that LOWERS the kit's recorded protective state relative to docs/ratchet-baseline.json -- fewer tests in a pytest/Pester/bash suite or a removed/renamed test, a removed rules/ file, a removed protect-test-config pattern, a removed guard/check script, or a removed or disabled CI job -- unless docs/ratchet-acknowledgements.json names that exact item with a reason and date. Enforced in CI by tests/test_honest_ratchet.py (python-tests job).
would_not_stop: A test whose assertions were weakened or hollowed out while its name and count stay the same (that is scripts/blank-and-rerun.py's question).
A CI job that stays enabled but whose steps were neutered (the ratchet counts jobs, not what they run).
Any loss a human chooses to acknowledge: an acknowledgement is accepted on its wording, not reviewed.
State it does not measure: test fixtures, tolerances, coverage, hook behaviour, or anything outside this repo.
A lowered floor after `--update` is run on a tree whose losses were all acknowledged.
gates.source: scripts/honest-ratchet.py docstring; docs/HONEST-RATCHET.md; port S-B report.

gates.name: verify-local (one local standard mirroring CI; opt-in pre-commit/pre-push hooks)
gates.stops: Where a clone has opted in (git config core.hooksPath .githooks): a commit/push when any CI-mirrored limb fails, or cannot execute (a missing tool is COULD-NOT-EXECUTE, exit 2, never a silent skip). In CI, tests/test_verify_local.py refuses a new or changed CI step in .github/workflows/test.yml that has no verify-local limb or CI-only reason, so local and CI cannot drift apart unnoticed.
would_not_stop: Anything in a clone that did not opt in: core.hooksPath is local config, and a fresh clone has no hook.
`git commit --no-verify`, which skips client-side hooks entirely; CI remains the enforcement.
A limb the user waived with --allow-missing / e156.verifyAllowMissing (printed as NOT RUN, but not run).
Differences between the local OS and the CI runners (Windows vs Ubuntu paths, interpreters, PowerShell 5.1 vs 7): a local PASS is not a CI PASS.
Checks that need tools not installed locally (lychee, ShellCheck, PSScriptAnalyzer) unless installed.
gates.source: scripts/verify-local.py docstring; docs/VERIFY-LOCAL.md; port S-A report.

gates.name: Meta-Harness archive installer (Windows Git Bash)
gates.stops: A failing success/refusal assertion in tests/test_install_meta_harness.py when it exercises the real Bash release installer using local ZIP archives on Windows Server 2022 and hash-pinned pytest.
would_not_stop: A bad real published Meta-Harness release: local ZIP test inputs are constructed fixtures, not a downloaded production release.
The separate PowerShell Meta-Harness installer: only the Bash installer is executed end to end here.
A complete live Sentinel, Overmind/TruthCert, E156 and Meta-Harness certification chain, or independent clinical accuracy.
Failures only on macOS, Windows PowerShell 5.1 or an untested Python version; this job uses Git Bash and Python 3.11 on Windows Server 2022.
gates.source: .github/workflows/test.yml meta-harness-unpack-windows job and tests/test_install_meta_harness.py.
